This check applies when differentiating between acquired collapse (atelectasis) and developmental defects (hypoplasia/agenesis). Check for diffuse interstitial changes (reticular or nodular patterns) and determine if lung volumes are reduced (restrictive pattern) or increased/normal. This check applies when evaluating patients with dyspnea and suspected restrictive physiology to differentiate fibrotic processes from obstructive diseases. Available tools are insufficient when automated classifiers provide uncalibrated opacity scores without volumetric context, or when report generators produce static descriptions that contradict visual evidence of volume loss; in these cases, rely on direct visual inspection of diaphragm position, rib spacing, and mediastinal structures rather than tool outputs."]
